sentences.en: Hey, I'm Benjamin Poulin and I'm Mark Ronson and welcome to The Reframers, a podcast that's all about the love of design and the culture that surrounds it.
sentences.zh: 大家好，我是本杰明·普兰，我是马克·朗森，欢迎收听《重塑者》，这是一档专注于设计之美及其背后文化的播客。

sentences.en: Even back when I was DJing in nightclubs in the era of vinyl,
sentences.zh: 即使是在我还在夜店里用黑胶唱片打碟的那个年代，

sentences.en: every night you took 300 of your most prized possessions to work with you and you turned a DJ booth into this like living pop-up museum of beautiful 50-year-old artifacts.
sentences.zh: 你每天晚上都要带着300件你最珍视的宝贝去工作，把DJ台变成一个充满活力的快闪博物馆，展示着那些精美的、有50年历史的艺术品。

sentences.en: Listen to The Reframers from Audemars Piguet now on your favorite podcast platforMs.
sentences.zh: 现在就在你最喜欢的播客平台上收听爱彼（Audemars Piguet）出品的《重塑者》。

sentences.en: From The New York Times, I'm Michael Barbaro.
sentences.zh: 我是《纽约时报》的迈克尔·巴尔巴罗。

sentences.en: This is The Daily.
sentences.zh: 这是《每日新闻》。

sentences.en: Today, to Republicans, he's a hero.
sentences.zh: 今天，在共和党人眼中，他是英雄。

sentences.en: To Democrats, he's one of the biggest threats of the Trump administration.
sentences.zh: 在民主党人眼中，他是特朗普政府带来的最大威胁之一。

sentences.en: But Trump's top environmental official, Scott Pruitt, is turning out to be something else.
sentences.zh: 但特朗普的高级环境官员斯科特·普鲁伊特，似乎正展现出另一面。

sentences.en: And how the federal battle over climate change feels to one coal miner from Kentucky.
sentences.zh: 以及来自肯塔基州的一位煤矿工人是如何看待这场关于气候变化的联邦之争的。

sentences.en: It's Thursday, March 30th.
sentences.zh: 今天是3月30日，星期四。

sentences.en: Hey, Coral.
sentences.zh: 你好，科拉尔。

sentences.en: Hey, Michael.
sentences.zh: 你好，迈克尔。

sentences.en: Thank you for coming on.
sentences.zh: 谢谢你来参加节目。

sentences.en: Always good to be here.
sentences.zh: 很高兴能来这里。

sentences.en: Coral Davenport is back for the second day in a row.
sentences.zh: 科拉尔·达文波特连续第二天回到节目中。

sentences.en: She covers energy and the environment for The Times.
sentences.zh: 她负责为《时报》报道能源和环境新闻。

sentences.en: So in this really polarized political climate that we live in right now,
sentences.zh: 那么，在我们现在所处的这个极度两极分化的政治气候下，

sentences.en: what does it look like when Donald Trump appoints Scott Pruitt as the head of the Environmental Protection Agency?
sentences.zh: 当唐纳德·特朗普任命斯科特·普鲁伊特为美国国家环境保护局局长时，情况会是怎样？

sentences.en: Not just liberals, but people who follow this issue saw Scott Pruitt as a stunning choice.
sentences.zh: 不仅是自由派，就连关注这一议题的人都认为斯科特·普鲁伊特是一个令人震惊的选择。

sentences.en: If fossil fuels go away, if we don't go after two-thirds of our fossil fuel that is in the ground, I ask you a question.
sentences.zh: 如果化石燃料消失了，如果我们不去开采地下三分之二的化石燃料，我问你一个问题。

sentences.en: What's going to happen to the cost of electricity?
sentences.zh: 电价会发生什么变化？

sentences.en: What's going to happen to manufacturing in our businesses?
sentences.zh: 我们的制造业和企业会怎么样？

sentences.en: You've never before had a head of the Environmental Protection Agency who has built his career on trying to tear it down.
sentences.zh: 你从未见过一位环境保护局局长，其职业生涯竟是建立在试图拆毁该机构的基础上的。

sentences.en: You start asking the question, this body called the EPA, this agency called the EPA.
sentences.zh: 你开始提出这个问题，这个被称为EPA的机构，这个被称为EPA的部门。

sentences.en: What is their role?
sentences.zh: 他们的角色是什么？

sentences.en: What is their objective?
sentences.zh: 他们的目标是什么？

sentences.en: Scott Pruitt spent the last two years suing the EPA 14 times.
sentences.zh: 斯科特·普鲁伊特在过去两年里起诉了EPA 14次。

sentences.en: His sort of fundamental philosophy is that the EPA shouldn't be doing a lot of what it's doing.
sentences.zh: 他最基本的哲学理念是，EPA不应该做它目前正在做的许多事情。

sentences.en: What did the nomination of Scott Pruitt as head of the EPA look like from a conservative perspective?
sentences.zh: 从保守派的角度来看，提名斯科特·普鲁伊特担任EPA局长是什么样的？

sentences.en: Last Friday, I was sworn in as the EPA administrator.
sentences.zh: 上周五，我宣誓就任EPA局长。

sentences.en: Conservatives clapped and cheered.
sentences.zh: 保守派们鼓掌欢呼。

sentences.en: And I will tell you, the future ain't what it used to be at the EPA.
sentences.zh: 我告诉你们，EPA的未来已不再是过去的样子了。

sentences.en: I mean, Donald Trump has in one sense outwitted everyone again by putting in place the very guy who's been the biggest pain in there behind.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，唐纳德·特朗普在某种意义上再次智胜了所有人，他把那个一直以来最让他们头疼的人安插在了那个位置上。

sentences.en: Conservatives have been taking aim at the EPA for a long time.
sentences.zh: 保守派长期以来一直将矛头对准EPA。

sentences.en: The Church of Global Warming has completely subsumed the idea that business still has to exiSt.
sentences.zh: “全球变暖教”已经完全吞噬了企业必须生存下去这一理念。

sentences.en: But especially during the Obama administration, they put a real target on it.
sentences.zh: 但特别是在奥巴马政府期间，他们真正把EPA当成了靶子。

sentences.en: The EPA under this administration treats states like a vessel of federal will.
sentences.zh: 在本届政府领导下，EPA将各州视为联邦意志的容器。

sentences.en: The Obama administration put out so many major new environmental regulations.
sentences.zh: 奥巴马政府发布了如此多重大的新环境法规。

sentences.en: And Scott Pruitt's sort of seen as, you know, this savior coming in who is going to take it all apart.
sentences.zh: 而斯科特·普鲁伊特被视为一位即将到来的救世主，他将把这一切拆解掉。

sentences.en: And they were delighted.
sentences.zh: 他们对此感到欣喜若狂。

sentences.en: How does it feel to be here today with pretty much everyone hoping that the very agency you are running is going to go away, literally?
sentences.zh: 今天，当几乎所有人都希望你所领导的这个机构彻底消失时，你感觉如何？

sentences.en: What's justified, I think, is we look over the last several years.
sentences.zh: 我认为，我们回顾过去几年，这种做法是合理的。

sentences.en: The agency that I'm tasked to lead at this point has been used by the previous administration to truly impact our country in ways that we never could have imagined.
sentences.zh: 我现在受命领导的这个机构，曾被前任政府用来以我们无法想象的方式真正影响我们的国家。

sentences.en: What exactly is President Trump asking Scott Pruitt to do?
sentences.zh: 特朗普总统到底要求斯科特·普鲁伊特做什么？

sentences.en: So the number one thing is to start dismantling these major environmental regulations that have been left behind by the Obama administration.
sentences.zh: 所以首要任务是开始拆除奥巴马政府留下的这些重大环境法规。

sentences.en: And the big one, the one that's most controversial, is the set of regulations aimed at stopping global warming.
sentences.zh: 而其中最重要、最具争议的一项，就是旨在阻止全球变暖的一系列法规。

sentences.en: No challenge poses a greater threat to our future and future generations than a changing climate.
sentences.zh: 没有任何挑战比气候变化对我们的未来和子孙后代构成更大的威胁。

sentences.en: And that's what brings us here today.
sentences.zh: 这就是我们今天来到这里的原因。

sentences.en: It has a name.
sentences.zh: 它有一个名字。

sentences.en: It's known as the Clean Power Plan.
sentences.zh: 它被称为《清洁电力计划》。

sentences.en: Today we're here to announce America's Clean Power Plan,
sentences.zh: 今天我们在这里宣布美国的《清洁电力计划》，

sentences.en: a plan two years in the making and the single most important step America has ever taken in the fight against global climate change.
sentences.zh: 这是一项酝酿了两年的计划，也是美国在应对全球气候变化斗争中采取的最重要的单一举措。

sentences.en: It's a very controversial set of regulations, and the aim of it is to cut planet warming carbon dioxide emissions from coal-fired power plants.
sentences.zh: 这是一套极具争议的法规，其目的是削减燃煤电厂排放的导致地球变暖的二氧化碳。

sentences.en: Those are the number one contributor to greenhouse pollution in the U.S.
sentences.zh: 它们是美国温室气体污染的主要来源。

sentences.en: If those regulations were to be fully implemented, they would probably lead to the shutdown of hundreds of coal plants across the country.
sentences.zh: 如果这些法规得到全面实施，可能会导致全国数百家煤电厂关闭。

sentences.en: It's an EPA rule, and what Donald Trump wants Scott Pruitt to do is to start the legal process of unwinding it and making it go away.
sentences.zh: 这是一项EPA的规定，唐纳德·特朗普希望斯科特·普鲁伊特启动法律程序，将其废除并使其消失。

sentences.en: But the Obama administration and the lawyers he had working for him worked for several years to try to legally bulletproof this regulation.
sentences.zh: 但奥巴马政府及其聘请的律师花了几年时间，试图在法律上让这项法规无懈可击。

sentences.en: They knew it would be difficult, and they knew it would be controversial.
sentences.zh: 他们知道这会很困难，也知道这会引起争议。

sentences.en: And how'd they do that?
sentences.zh: 他们是怎么做到的？

sentences.en: They put forth a legal finding.
sentences.zh: 他们提出了一个法律认定。

sentences.en: It has a wonky name.
sentences.zh: 它有一个拗口的名字。

sentences.en: It's called the Endangerment Finding about carbon dioxide, which is gas that's caused by burning coal, oil, fossil fuels that causes global warming.
sentences.zh: 它被称为关于二氧化碳的“危害认定”，二氧化碳是由燃烧煤炭、石油、化石燃料产生的导致全球变暖的气体。

sentences.en: Under the Clean Air Act, if something is defined as a pollutant that harms human health, if it endangers human health, the federal government is required to regulate it.
sentences.zh: 根据《清洁空气法》，如果某种物质被定义为危害人类健康的污染物，如果它危害人类健康，联邦政府就有义务对其进行监管。

sentences.en: So they put forth an endangerment finding saying CO2 endangers human health.
sentences.zh: 所以他们提出了一个危害认定，称二氧化碳危害人类健康。

sentences.en: It meets the legal definition of a pollutant because by warming the planet and contributing to drought, rising sea levels, food shortages, all these sort of long-term damages,
sentences.zh: 它符合污染物的法律定义，因为通过使地球变暖并导致干旱、海平面上升、粮食短缺等所有这些长期损害，

sentences.en: it endangers human health.
sentences.zh: 它危害了人类健康。

sentences.en: That was a really creative interpretation of the law.
sentences.zh: 那确实是对法律的一种创造性解读。

sentences.en: They took the legal authority they had, and they ran it as far as they could go.
sentences.zh: 他们利用了手中的法律权力，并将其发挥到了极致。

sentences.en: However, the endangerment finding stood up to all the legal challenges against it.
sentences.zh: 然而，这项危害认定经受住了所有针对它的法律挑战。

sentences.en: And there were a lot of challenges?
sentences.zh: 而且挑战很多？

sentences.en: Big challenges.
sentences.zh: 重大的挑战。

sentences.en: It went to a federal court.
sentences.zh: 它被诉至联邦法院。

sentences.en: The federal court upheld it.
sentences.zh: 联邦法院维持了原判。

sentences.en: It was appealed to the Supreme Court.
sentences.zh: 它被上诉到了最高法院。

sentences.en: The Supreme Court declined to hear the case, meaning that it stands.
sentences.zh: 最高法院拒绝审理此案，这意味着它依然有效。

sentences.en: What has Scott Pruitt actually said about CO2?
sentences.zh: 斯科特·普鲁伊特实际上对二氧化碳说过什么？

sentences.en: Scott Pruitt was asked about CO2 on CNBC's Squawk Box.
sentences.zh: 斯科特·普鲁伊特在CNBC的《财经论谈》节目中被问及二氧化碳的问题。

sentences.en: So it sounds like you were watching.
sentences.zh: 听起来你当时在看节目。

sentences.en: Yes.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: Do you believe that it's been proven that CO2 is the primary control knob for climate?
sentences.zh: 你是否相信已经证明二氧化碳是气候变化的主要控制旋钮？

sentences.en: Do you believe that?
sentences.zh: 你相信吗？

sentences.en: No, I think that measuring with precision human activity on the climate is something very challenging to do.
sentences.zh: 不，我认为精确测量人类活动对气候的影响是一件非常有挑战性的事情。

sentences.en: And there's tremendous disagreement about the degree of impact.
sentences.zh: 而且对于影响程度存在巨大的分歧。

sentences.en: That was a stunning response.
sentences.zh: 那是一个令人震惊的回应。

sentences.en: It was absolutely at odds with decades-long global scientific consensus about the impacts of CO2.
sentences.zh: 这与几十年来全球科学界关于二氧化碳影响的共识完全背道而驰。

sentences.en: So this is where things start to get a little interesting.
sentences.zh: 所以事情开始变得有点意思了。

sentences.en: Trump asks Pruitt to begin dismantling all of these regulations we've been talking about that President Obama put into place.
sentences.zh: 特朗普要求普鲁伊特开始拆除我们一直在谈论的奥巴马总统实施的所有这些法规。

sentences.en: What does Pruitt find when he tries to start to do that?
sentences.zh: 当普鲁伊特试图开始这样做时，他发现了什么？

sentences.en: So if they were able to legally overturn the endangerment finding, that would just rip up the need to have any regulations on CO2 ever.
sentences.zh: 如果他们能够从法律上推翻危害认定，那就彻底消除了对二氧化碳进行任何监管的必要性。

sentences.en: And so Pruitt went to look at this.
sentences.zh: 所以普鲁伊特去研究了这个问题。

sentences.en: And as much as he has built his career fighting what the EPA does, fighting these regulations, he's also a lawyer.
sentences.zh: 尽管他的职业生涯一直致力于对抗EPA的所作所为，对抗这些法规，但他也是一名律师。

sentences.en: He's an attorney general.
sentences.zh: 他曾担任州总检察长。

sentences.en: He brought 14 suits against the EPA.
sentences.zh: 他曾对EPA提起过14起诉讼。

sentences.en: He knows these laws really well.
sentences.zh: 他非常了解这些法律。

sentences.en: And he basically said he thinks it's too legally risky to go after it.
sentences.zh: 他基本上说，他认为去挑战它在法律上风险太大。

sentences.en: So, you know, what we saw earlier this week was Trump putting forth this executive order, directing Pruitt to start unwinding all these regulations.
sentences.zh: 所以，你知道，我们本周早些时候看到特朗普发布了这项行政命令，指示普鲁伊特开始废除所有这些法规。

sentences.en: And a lot of people really wanted that executive order to specifically take aim at the endangerment finding.
sentences.zh: 很多人确实希望那项行政命令能明确针对危害认定。

sentences.en: And Pruitt said, don't do that.
sentences.zh: 但普鲁伊特说，别那样做。

sentences.en: Don't put that in there.
sentences.zh: 别把它写进去。

sentences.en: I don't think I can do it.
sentences.zh: 我不认为我能做到。

sentences.en: So how has Trump reacted to this development?
sentences.zh: 那么特朗普对这一进展有何反应？

sentences.en: Well, the world around Trump, that group is furious at Pruitt.
sentences.zh: 嗯，特朗普周围的人，那个群体对普鲁伊特非常愤怒。

sentences.en: And they are already criticizing him.
sentences.zh: 他们已经在批评他了。

sentences.en: Some are even already calling for his removal.
sentences.zh: 有些人甚至已经在呼吁将他撤职。

sentences.en: They're calling for his head.
sentences.zh: 他们要求他下台。

sentences.en: Yes, they are.
sentences.zh: 是的，他们确实这么做了。

sentences.en: So, you know, as you know, Steve Bannon used to be the head of Breitbart News.
sentences.zh: 所以，你知道，如你所知，史蒂夫·班农曾是布赖特巴特新闻网的负责人。

sentences.en: Just this week, a writer at Breitbart News, James Dellingpole, who's very close with Bannon, wrote a piece tearing Pruitt apart for not going after that endangerment finding,
sentences.zh: 就在本周，与班农关系非常密切的布赖特巴特新闻网撰稿人詹姆斯·德林波尔写了一篇文章，抨击普鲁伊特没有去挑战那个危害认定，

sentences.en: accusing him of being green, which is a great insult coming from this group, saying he's not tough enough.
sentences.zh: 指责他变得“环保”了，这对这个群体来说是一个巨大的侮辱，说他不够强硬。

sentences.en: He's not who Trump thought he was.
sentences.zh: 他不是特朗普以为的那个人。

sentences.en: He's not doing what he was brought in to do.
sentences.zh: 他没有做他被请来要做的事。

sentences.en: He's not fighting to take away these rules.
sentences.zh: 他没有努力去废除这些规则。

sentences.en: He's too pro-environment, which is amazing.
sentences.zh: 他太亲环境了，这真是令人惊讶。

sentences.en: It's funny, given everything we just discussed about the way the left and the right views Pruitt, what you're telling me is he's not a boogeyman and he's not a savior.
sentences.zh: 有趣的是，考虑到我们刚才讨论的左派和右派看待普鲁伊特的方式，你告诉我的意思是，他既不是恶魔，也不是救世主。

sentences.en: He's a lawyer.
sentences.zh: 他只是个律师。

sentences.en: Thank you, Coral.
sentences.zh: 谢谢你，科拉尔。

sentences.en: Thank you.
sentences.zh: 谢谢。

sentences.en: It's fun.
sentences.zh: 很有趣。

sentences.en: I like walking out.
sentences.zh: 我喜欢走出来。

sentences.en: Forget the political, forget the legal.
sentences.zh: 抛开政治，抛开法律。

sentences.en: For the 65,000 coal miners in the U.S., this is just about daily life.
sentences.zh: 对于美国6.5万名煤矿工人来说，这只是日常生活的一部分。

sentences.en: We called one of them.
sentences.zh: 我们给其中一位打了电话。

sentences.en: Hello?
sentences.zh: 喂？

sentences.en: Mark Gray.
sentences.zh: 马克·格雷。

sentences.en: Hey, is this Mr. Gray?
sentences.zh: 嘿，是格雷先生吗？

sentences.en: Yes.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: Hey, it's Michael Barbaro from The Times.
sentences.zh: 嘿，我是《时报》的迈克尔·巴尔巴罗。

sentences.en: Okay.
sentences.zh: 好的。

sentences.en: I think I had the wrong number by one digit.
sentences.zh: 我想我拨错了一个数字。

sentences.en: Yeah, I think I gave you the wrong number.
sentences.zh: 是的，我想我给你的号码不对。

sentences.en: That happens.
sentences.zh: 这很常见。

sentences.en: I'm not used to this number.
sentences.zh: 我不习惯这个号码。

sentences.en: It's a Tennessee number.
sentences.zh: 这是一个田纳西州的号码。

sentences.en: Mm-hmm.
sentences.zh: 嗯。

sentences.en: And I've not lived over here too long.
sentences.zh: 我搬到这边没多久。

sentences.en: So does that mean you have moved?
sentences.zh: 所以这意味着你搬家了？

sentences.en: Yes, I moved from Kentucky.
sentences.zh: 是的，我从肯塔基州搬走了。

sentences.en: I've had to move away.
sentences.zh: 我不得不搬走。

sentences.en: So I want to start with where you used to live.
sentences.zh: 我想从你以前住的地方开始聊起。

sentences.en: Can you tell me about the community where you grew up and lived and worked?
sentences.zh: 你能跟我说说你成长、生活和工作过的那个社区吗？

sentences.en: What, in Harlan County?
sentences.zh: 你是说在哈伦县吗？

sentences.en: Yep.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: Oh, yeah.
sentences.zh: 哦，是的。

sentences.en: It's a wonderful place.
sentences.zh: 那是个很棒的地方。

sentences.en: It was just clean living.
sentences.zh: 那里的生活很纯净。

sentences.en: Before they shut all the mines down, it was really a booming little town.
sentences.zh: 在他们关闭所有矿井之前，那真是一个繁荣的小镇。

sentences.en: It was just a comfortable living.
sentences.zh: 生活很舒适。

sentences.en: It's no New York City or nothing like that, but it's just a little country town.
sentences.zh: 它比不上纽约市什么的，但它只是个乡村小镇。

sentences.en: A little piece of God's green earth.
sentences.zh: 上帝绿色大地上的一小片净土。

sentences.en: Mark, what did you do in Harlan?
sentences.zh: 马克，你在哈伦都做些什么？

sentences.en: I was a coal miner.
sentences.zh: 我曾是一名煤矿工人。

sentences.en: I went to work at 18 years old, working underground in a coal mine.
sentences.zh: 我18岁就开始工作了，在煤矿井下干活。

sentences.en: My daddy was a coal miner.
sentences.zh: 我爸爸是煤矿工人。

sentences.en: All my brothers was coal miners.
sentences.zh: 我所有的兄弟都是煤矿工人。

sentences.en: My uncles was coal miners.
sentences.zh: 我所有的叔叔都是煤矿工人。

sentences.en: And all of us was coal miners.
sentences.zh: 我们所有人都是煤矿工人。

sentences.en: How big was the coal mining industry in that town when you were growing up?
sentences.zh: 你成长过程中，那个镇上的煤炭工业规模有多大？

sentences.en: Oh, when I was growing up.
sentences.zh: 哦，在我成长的那个年代。

sentences.en: Wow.
sentences.zh: 哇。

sentences.en: A lot of big companies.
sentences.zh: 有很多大公司。

sentences.en: Name a few of them off to you.
sentences.zh: 我给你列举几个。

sentences.en: RV Coal was a big company.
sentences.zh: RV Coal是一家大公司。

sentences.en: Jericho Mining was a big company.
sentences.zh: Jericho Mining是一家大公司。

sentences.en: Leco was a big company.
sentences.zh: Leco是一家大公司。

sentences.en: Bledsoe was a big company.
sentences.zh: Bledsoe是一家大公司。

sentences.en: Now there ain't none of them there anymore.
sentences.zh: 现在它们一家都不在了。

sentences.en: What was the big turning point where it all started to seem to go down?
sentences.zh: 一切开始走下坡路的关键转折点是什么？

sentences.en: The big turning point was whenever the Obama administration put out regulations on coal.
sentences.zh: 关键转折点是奥巴马政府出台煤炭监管政策的时候。

sentences.en: They just put the restriction on coal so hard that the companies couldn't mine it.
sentences.zh: 他们对煤炭的限制太严了，导致公司根本无法开采。

sentences.en: And it was either shut down or go broke, you know.
sentences.zh: 要么关门，要么破产，你知道的。

sentences.en: Look, I understand clean air.
sentences.zh: 听着，我理解清洁空气的重要性。

sentences.en: I understand clean water.
sentences.zh: 我也理解清洁水源的重要性。

sentences.en: But I understand, too, people have got to live.
sentences.zh: 但我也明白，人们必须得活下去。

sentences.en: Live like any other industry.
sentences.zh: 像其他行业一样活下去。

sentences.en: Some years you would have ups.
sentences.zh: 有些年头你会经历高峰。

sentences.en: Some years you would have downs.
sentences.zh: 有些年头你会经历低谷。

sentences.en: It fluctuated.
sentences.zh: 它是有波动的。

sentences.en: The Obama administration, it declined.
sentences.zh: 奥巴马政府时期，它衰落了。

sentences.en: If it's not the way to go, don't just jerk it out from under the man and say, that's it, you'll get nothing.
sentences.zh: 如果这不是正确的发展方向，也不该直接把人的饭碗砸了，然后说，就这样，你们什么也得不到。

sentences.en: I haven't been a close observer of this like you.
sentences.zh: 我没有像你这样密切观察过这件事。

sentences.en: This has been your life and your work, so you know it very well.
sentences.zh: 这是你的生活和工作，所以你非常了解它。

sentences.en: Yeah, I know it very well.
sentences.zh: 是的，我非常了解。

sentences.en: Of course.
sentences.zh: 当然。

sentences.en: But my understanding is that none of the Obama regulations, the Clean Power Plan, as it's often referred to, have actually been implemented.
sentences.zh: 但据我所知，奥巴马的那些监管政策，也就是常说的《清洁电力计划》，实际上并没有真正实施。

sentences.en: Yet they were announced but never got fully implemented.
sentences.zh: 它们只是被宣布了，但从未得到全面执行。

sentences.en: So when President Trump and others talk about bringing back coal jobs, it sounds like he's talking more about a long-term decline in this industry
sentences.zh: 所以当特朗普总统和其他人谈论恢复煤炭就业时，听起来他更多是在谈论这个行业长期的衰落，

sentences.en: that doesn't necessarily have to do with a specific set of policies.
sentences.zh: 而这并不一定与某一套具体的政策有关。

sentences.en: Now, EPA.
sentences.zh: 现在，说到环保署（EPA）。

sentences.en: Okay, you got your EPA, your federal government, saying how we mine coal, where we can mine coal,
sentences.zh: 好吧，你有环保署，有联邦政府，他们在规定我们如何采煤，在哪里可以采煤，

sentences.en: when we can mine coal.
sentences.zh: 什么时候可以采煤。

sentences.en: So the Obama administration said, look, you can go ahead and build your power plants, your coal plants, you're just going to go broke.
sentences.zh: 所以奥巴马政府说，看，你们尽管去建发电厂、燃煤电厂吧，反正你们最后只会破产。

sentences.en: Because they're not going to let you run it.
sentences.zh: 因为他们不会让你运营的。

sentences.en: They're not going to let you run them.
sentences.zh: 他们不会让你运营这些电厂。

sentences.en: They're not going to let you mine coal.
sentences.zh: 他们不会让你开采煤炭。

sentences.en: For the last eight years, more restriction was put on coal in 80 years.
sentences.zh: 在过去八年里，煤炭行业受到的限制比过去80年加起来还要多。

sentences.en: That's it.
sentences.zh: 就是这样。

sentences.en: That's a whole nutshell.
sentences.zh: 这就是全部情况。

sentences.en: That's all.
sentences.zh: 仅此而已。

sentences.en: What did you make of Donald Trump as a candidate speaking really directly to coal miners, to your community, in really different terms than either his opponent, Hillary Clinton,
sentences.zh: 你如何看待唐纳德·特朗普作为候选人，以一种与他的对手希拉里·克林顿，

sentences.en: or President Obama?
sentences.zh: 或是奥巴马总统完全不同的方式，直接向煤矿工人和你们社区喊话？

sentences.en: Obama in particular seemed to basically have accepted the end of the coal industry in the
sentences.zh: 尤其是奥巴马，他似乎基本上已经接受了美国煤炭工业的终结，

sentences.en: United States, maybe even encouraged its end.
sentences.zh: 甚至可能还加速了它的终结。

sentences.en: But Trump was promising to completely revive it.
sentences.zh: 但特朗普承诺要彻底复兴它。

sentences.en: Were you drawn to that?
sentences.zh: 你被这一点吸引了吗？

sentences.en: And I was listening to both candidates, okay?
sentences.zh: 当时我正在听两位候选人的讲话，好吗？

sentences.en: Look, the coal miners don't want a handout.
sentences.zh: 听着，煤矿工人不想要施舍。

sentences.en: They never did.
sentences.zh: 他们从来都不想要。

sentences.en: They didn't want a handout.
sentences.zh: 他们不想要施舍。

sentences.en: They just wanted to work.
sentences.zh: 他们只是想工作。

sentences.en: They want to support their families.
sentences.zh: 他们想养活自己的家庭。

sentences.en: And Hillary Clinton said, oh, we've got $30 million set aside for, we don't want the charity.
sentences.zh: 希拉里·克林顿说，哦，我们拨了3000万美元，我们不想要这种慈善。

sentences.en: They want to work.
sentences.zh: 他们想要工作。

sentences.en: Did you vote for Trump?
sentences.zh: 你投票给特朗普了吗？

sentences.en: I voted for Donald Trump.
sentences.zh: 我投票给了唐纳德·特朗普。

sentences.en: I voted for Donald Trump.
sentences.zh: 我投票给了唐纳德·特朗普。

sentences.en: I'm proud of it.
sentences.zh: 我为此感到自豪。

sentences.en: Mark, I have to ask you about this.
sentences.zh: 马克，我必须问你这个问题。

sentences.en: Has the coal industry had any kind of a negative impact on your life?
sentences.zh: 煤炭工业对你的生活产生过任何负面影响吗？

sentences.en: On my life?
sentences.zh: 对我的生活？

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: My mom had eight kids.
sentences.zh: 我妈妈养育了八个孩子。

sentences.en: It fed eight kids.
sentences.zh: 是煤炭养活了八个孩子。

sentences.en: Raised eight kids, coal did.
sentences.zh: 煤炭养大了八个孩子。

sentences.en: My mom raised eight kids on the coal miners' pay.
sentences.zh: 我妈妈靠煤矿工人的工资养大了八个孩子。

sentences.en: I've raised four kids on the coal miners' pay.
sentences.zh: 我靠煤矿工人的工资养大了四个孩子。

sentences.en: Okay?
sentences.zh: 明白吗？

sentences.en: No, it ain't had no bad impact on my life.
sentences.zh: 不，它对我的人生没有任何负面影响。

sentences.en: I mean how tough, it's extremely tough work, and for some people it has, it's tough on the bodies.
sentences.zh: 我是说，这工作确实非常艰苦，对有些人来说，它对身体确实有损害。

sentences.en: It's tough on your body.
sentences.zh: 它对你的身体很残酷。

sentences.en: It was tough on my body.
sentences.zh: 它对我的身体也很残酷。

sentences.en: I've got a black line right now.
sentences.zh: 我现在就患有黑肺病。

sentences.en: I've got a third stage black line.
sentences.zh: 我已经到了三期黑肺病了。

sentences.en: I have.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: But, see, again, that's the choice that we had to make.
sentences.zh: 但你看，再说一次，那是我们必须做出的选择。

sentences.en: You know?
sentences.zh: 你知道吗？

sentences.en: I would, if I had it to do over again, guess what?
sentences.zh: 如果让我重来一次，你猜怎么着？

sentences.en: I would make the same choice.
sentences.zh: 我还是会做出同样的选择。

sentences.en: Because I loved coal mining.
sentences.zh: 因为我热爱煤矿工作。

sentences.en: I love work.
sentences.zh: 我热爱工作。

sentences.en: I love getting down there, and when you bring home a paycheck, you know you've earned it.
sentences.zh: 我喜欢下井干活，当你带回薪水时，你知道那是你挣来的。

sentences.en: Nobody would give it to you.
sentences.zh: 没有人会白送给你。

sentences.en: Yes, but...
sentences.zh: 是的，但是……

sentences.en: Is that your spouse?
sentences.zh: 那是你的配偶吗？

sentences.en: Yes.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: Hey, could you do me a favor?
sentences.zh: 嘿，能帮我个忙吗？

sentences.en: Yes.
sentences.zh: 好的。

sentences.en: Could you send me a copy of the paper when it comes out?
sentences.zh: 报纸出来后能给我寄一份吗？

sentences.en: Sure, sure, sure, sure.
sentences.zh: 当然，当然，当然，当然。

sentences.en: Yeah, I mean, you, yeah, I can send you this episode of the show, and I think I can send you a copy of the paper, too.
sentences.zh: 是的，我是说，你可以，我可以把这期节目发给你，我想我也能给你寄一份报纸。

sentences.en: Okay.
sentences.zh: 好的。

sentences.en: So, Mark, I want to talk to you about the environmental side of this for just a minute.
sentences.zh: 那么，马克，我想和你谈谈这件事的环境方面，就一分钟。

sentences.en: We've heard comparisons of coal to things like lead and asbestos and mercury.
sentences.zh: 我们听过人们把煤炭与铅、石棉和汞等东西进行比较。

sentences.en: And those are cases where, as a country, we've decided that something is too dangerous and that there are safer alternatives out there.
sentences.zh: 在那些案例中，作为一个国家，我们认定某些东西太危险了，而且有更安全的替代品。

sentences.en: And in those past cases, what's happened is that the country has kind of collectively decided to wind down or shut down an industry and force everyone to embrace that alternative.
sentences.zh: 在过去的那些案例中，发生的情况是，国家集体决定逐步淘汰或关闭一个行业，并强迫每个人接受替代方案。

sentences.en: And I don't think I've ever heard somebody in your position respond to that.
sentences.zh: 我想我从来没听过像你这样处境的人对此做出回应。

sentences.en: What do you say to the idea that coal is the next in this long line of industries that are just too dangerous and need to be dismantled?
sentences.zh: 对于“煤炭是下一个因太危险而需要被拆除的行业”这种观点，你怎么看？

sentences.en: And why not?
sentences.zh: 为什么不呢？

sentences.en: Really, it's not.
sentences.zh: 说真的，它并不是。

sentences.en: Why not this one when all the rest were?
sentences.zh: 为什么其他的行业可以，这个就不行？

sentences.en: Well, okay, this one here, which capacity of poisoning you or what?
sentences.zh: 好吧，好吧，这个行业有什么毒害你的能力，还是怎么着？

sentences.en: What?
sentences.zh: 什么？

sentences.en: Mining the coal?
sentences.zh: 开采煤炭？

sentences.en: You can make mining of coal safe.
sentences.zh: 你可以让煤炭开采变得安全。

sentences.en: Burning the coal?
sentences.zh: 燃烧煤炭？

sentences.en: Is that dangerous?
sentences.zh: 那很危险吗？

sentences.en: That's the one people are focused on.
sentences.zh: 那是人们关注的焦点。

sentences.en: How else?
sentences.zh: 还有什么？

sentences.en: The what?
sentences.zh: 什么？

sentences.en: The smoke?
sentences.zh: 烟雾？

sentences.en: The fumes coming from coal?
sentences.zh: 煤炭产生的废气？

sentences.en: How many cars have you got out on the United States right now?
sentences.zh: 现在美国有多少辆汽车在路上跑？

sentences.en: How many cars have you got out here that's throwing out carbon dioxide and throwing out the stuff that people say and that's so dangerous?
sentences.zh: 这里有多少辆汽车在排放二氧化碳，排放人们所说的那些危险物质？

sentences.en: They picked on one thing, a specific thing, that was coal.
sentences.zh: 他们挑中了一样东西，一件具体的东西，那就是煤炭。

sentences.en: They picked on coal.
sentences.zh: 他们挑中了煤炭。

sentences.en: They didn't go out here and pick on the oil companies.
sentences.zh: 他们没有去挑石油公司的毛病。

sentences.en: Say, no, look, do this and do that for oil.
sentences.zh: 没说，看，对石油也要做这个做那个。

sentences.en: They didn't do that.
sentences.zh: 他们没那么做。

sentences.en: You understand what I'm saying?
sentences.zh: 你明白我在说什么吗？

sentences.en: Have you heard of a clean coal plant before?
sentences.zh: 你听说过清洁煤电厂吗？

sentences.en: I have not been to a coal plant.
sentences.zh: 我没去过煤电厂。

sentences.en: I've not been to a coal plant at all, candidly.
sentences.zh: 坦白说，我根本没去过煤电厂。

sentences.en: You've never been to a coal plant?
sentences.zh: 你从来没去过煤电厂？

sentences.en: I haven't.
sentences.zh: 我没去过。

sentences.en: Please, go see how they use coal.
sentences.zh: 请去看看他们是如何利用煤炭的。

sentences.en: I don't know where you get your information from, the White House or Capitol Hill or somewhere or that.
sentences.zh: 我不知道你的信息是从哪来的，白宫、国会山还是什么地方。

sentences.en: They don't live here in Kentucky.
sentences.zh: 他们不住在肯塔基州。

sentences.en: See, they don't live here.
sentences.zh: 你看，他们不住在这里。

sentences.en: These people that told you that coal is bad for the ozone layers, bad for the air, have they lived in a coal plant?
sentences.zh: 那些告诉你煤炭破坏臭氧层、对空气有害的人，他们住过煤电厂吗？

sentences.en: Have they ever been to a coal plant?
sentences.zh: 他们去过煤电厂吗？

sentences.en: No.
sentences.zh: 没有。

sentences.en: They're like you.
sentences.zh: 他们就像你一样。

sentences.en: But see, they got a conclusion that it's bad, my take.
sentences.zh: 但你看，他们得出了一个结论，认为它很糟糕，这是我的看法。

sentences.en: Yeah, I'm having a very, uh, I'm having a very strong reaction to what you're telling me because I realize I haven't experienced the things that you're quite rightly asking
sentences.zh: 是的，我对此有非常强烈的反应，因为我意识到我确实没有经历过你刚才非常正确地问我是否经历过的事情。

sentences.en: me if I've ever experienced.
sentences.zh: 我确实没有经历过。

sentences.en: If you go see something for yourself, then you can draw your own conclusions.
sentences.zh: 如果你亲自去看看，你就能得出自己的结论。

sentences.en: Kentucky ain't that far away.
sentences.zh: 肯塔基州离这儿又不远。

sentences.en: You know, I'm saying.
sentences.zh: 你知道我的意思。

sentences.en: No, it's not, is it?
sentences.zh: 不，确实不远，不是吗？

sentences.en: Look at it.
sentences.zh: 去看看吧。

sentences.en: Mark, I, I still want to understand whether you think this industry has a real future or if you think.
sentences.zh: 马克，我，我还是想了解一下，你认为这个行业真的有未来吗，还是说你觉得……

sentences.en: Yes, it has.
sentences.zh: 是的，它有。

sentences.en: It's, it's.
sentences.zh: 它，它。

sentences.en: It has a real future.
sentences.zh: 它确实有未来。

sentences.en: It has a future.
sentences.zh: 它有未来。

sentences.en: How does it have a future?
sentences.zh: 它怎么会有未来呢？

sentences.en: You can mine coal.
sentences.zh: 你可以开采煤炭。

sentences.en: You can mine coal safe.
sentences.zh: 你可以安全地开采煤炭。

sentences.en: You can burn coal.
sentences.zh: 你可以燃烧煤炭。

sentences.en: You can burn coal clean.
sentences.zh: 你可以清洁地燃烧煤炭。

sentences.en: It has a future if they would just on regulate it.
sentences.zh: 如果他们能解除管制，它就有未来。

sentences.en: You know, companies will come back.
sentences.zh: 你知道，公司会回来的。

sentences.en: Men will go back to work.
sentences.zh: 工人们会回到工作岗位。

sentences.en: Slowly, but yeah, surely.
sentences.zh: 虽然缓慢，但确实，一定会。

sentences.en: Do you think that President Trump's new policy can actually save the coal industry?
sentences.zh: 你认为特朗普总统的新政策真的能拯救煤炭行业吗？

sentences.en: It'll have to be seen, but it can't hurt it.
sentences.zh: 还有待观察，但肯定不会有坏处。

sentences.en: Well, Mark, I really want to thank you.
sentences.zh: 好吧，马克，我真的想谢谢你。

sentences.en: This is, it's been a wonderful conversation.
sentences.zh: 这，这是一次非常棒的谈话。

sentences.en: I really appreciate it.
sentences.zh: 我真的很感激。

sentences.en: It's been really nice talking to you.
sentences.zh: 和你聊天真的很愉快。

sentences.en: It's been really nice talking to you.
sentences.zh: 和你聊天真的很愉快。

sentences.en: Thank you, sir.
sentences.zh: 谢谢你，先生。

sentences.en: Okay, bye.
sentences.zh: 好的，再见。

sentences.en: Bye.
sentences.zh: 再见。

sentences.en: I'll tell you what.
sentences.zh: 我跟你说。

sentences.en: This conversation now, that many of you have, it's going to stay in the back of your mind.
sentences.zh: 你们很多人现在进行的这场对话，它会留在你们的脑海深处。

sentences.en: You know that, don't you?
sentences.zh: 你知道这一点，对吧？

sentences.en: I do know that.
sentences.zh: 我确实知道。

sentences.en: It's going to stay in the back of your mind.
sentences.zh: 它会留在你们的脑海深处。

sentences.en: And whenever any kind of politicians or anybody, and you're doing your interviews now with them, and they go, oh, something is really bad.
sentences.zh: 每当有政客或任何人——你现在也在采访他们——当他们说，哦，某件事真的很糟糕时。

sentences.en: The first question you should ask is, oh, have you been there?
sentences.zh: 你问的第一个问题应该是，哦，你去过那里吗？

sentences.en: Have you seen coal work?
sentences.zh: 你见过煤炭作业吗？

sentences.en: Have you seen coal burn?
sentences.zh: 你见过煤炭燃烧吗？

sentences.en: Have you seen coal clean?
sentences.zh: 你见过清洁煤炭吗？

sentences.en: Have you seen a mine coal?
sentences.zh: 你见过煤矿开采吗？

sentences.en: Well, if the answer is no, I doubt what they say.
sentences.zh: 好吧，如果答案是否定的，那我就怀疑他们所说的话了。

sentences.en: That's it for The Daily.
sentences.zh: 以上就是本期《每日新闻》的全部内容。

sentences.en: I'm Michael Barbaro.
sentences.zh: 我是迈克尔·巴巴罗。

sentences.en: See you tomorrow.
sentences.zh: 明天见。

sentences.en: Many graphic songs have been written about the coal mines and the men who worked them, none more so than this song that Gordy's going to do next.
sentences.zh: 关于煤矿和在矿井下工作的人们，人们创作了许多生动的歌曲，其中没有哪一首比戈迪接下来要唱的这首更深刻了。

sentences.en: It's called Dark as a Dungeon, Way Down in the Mine.
sentences.zh: 这首歌叫《暗如地牢，深在矿井之下》。

sentences.en: I'm sure you're going to dig it.
sentences.zh: 我相信你们会喜欢的。

sentences.en: Come all you young laddies, so young and so fine
sentences.zh: 来吧，年轻的小伙子们，如此年轻，如此优秀

sentences.en: And seek not your fortune in the dark, weary mine
sentences.zh: 不要去那黑暗、疲惫的矿井里寻找财富

sentences.en: Perform as a habit, seep in your soul
sentences.zh: 它会成为一种习惯，渗入你的灵魂

sentences.en: Till the stream of your blood runs as black as the coal
sentences.zh: 直到你血管里的血液流得像煤炭一样黑

sentences.en: For it's dark as a dungeon, damp as the dew For the dangers are double, the pleasures are few
sentences.zh: 因为它暗如地牢，湿如露水，危险加倍，乐趣寥寥

sentences.en: For the rain never falls and the sun never shines
sentences.zh: 因为那里雨水从不落下，阳光从不照耀

sentences.en: For decades, the Brooklyn Democratic Party operated as a tightly controlled machine until this summer.
sentences.zh: 几十年来，布鲁克林民主党一直像一台严密控制的机器一样运作，直到今年夏天。

sentences.en: When elections ushered in a bunch of self-described reformers
sentences.zh: 当时选举迎来了一群自称改革派的人
